account:
Contributor 01 was assigned to investigate transcript timing for Project Lantern, a 12-recording pilot intended to make transcripts easier to follow during the spring evening programme. The pre-existing problem was manually produced cue sheets drifting after pauses; no earlier activity was found in the enumerated 90-day sweep. Contributor 01 proposed deriving boundaries from mastered audio while exposing weak alignments for review, then implemented the alignment command, confidence report, overlap prevention, tests, configurable threshold and provenance fields. The first evaluation covered only four recordings and 68 reviewed boundaries: median boundary error was 0.42 seconds, while two music sections remained poor. Contributor 07 identified the hard-coded threshold and missing provenance; Contributor 01 corrected both before merge.

Contributor 01 also operated the workflow: regenerating cues after Contributor 03 supplied editorial boundaries, investigating flags, detecting that recording J had been evaluated against a stale master, rerunning it against the replacement source, documenting its remaining exception, and supplying a fixture that helped Contributor 04 repair tablet flicker. The work was shared: Contributor 03 owned transcript corrections and listening decisions; Contributor 08 supplied export constraints and support; Contributor 04 owned player defects; Contributor 06 controlled release. The initial J result was discarded after the stale brief was confirmed, rather than counted as an alignment failure. Recording D required a manual editorial split, not a general improvement to Contributor 01's tool.

Ten reviewed recordings were released in March; K and L remained blocked on curatorial transcript approval and were never completed by the June horizon. This was not attributable to Contributor 01. Subsequent player defects were reproduced independently of generated cues and fixed by Contributor 04. In seven evening sessions, voluntary host logs recorded 11 transcript-related comments from approximately 510 audio starts: five wording requests, three early/late highlights, two larger-text requests and one unclear note. Those logs do not establish a true error rate. The ten recordings remained in the evening programme through June. A separate staff-training recording reused the runbook, demonstrating one use outside the pilot but not repeated adoption or a full accuracy assessment. Two editors reported reduced preparation effort, but time was not tracked. Broader collection adoption and visitor accessibility impact remained unmeasured.

claims.statement: Contributor 01 was assigned to investigate transcript timing, while player work and content testing belonged to Contributors 04 and 03 respectively.
claims.limits: This establishes the initial division of work, not sole ownership of Project Lantern.

claims.statement: The project addressed a pre-existing condition: manually produced cue sheets drifted after pauses. The enumerated 90-day earlier windows contained no roots in chat, docs or repo.
claims.limits: The empty bounded sweep does not prove that no older or unretained history existed.

claims.statement: Contributor 01 proposed deriving cue boundaries from mastered audio and returning confidence flags for weak alignment, preserving low-confidence items for editorial review.
claims.limits: Contributor 03 supplied the editorial-review constraint; the proposal was not a promise of fully automatic validation.

claims.statement: Contributor 01 implemented the alignment command, confidence report, overlap prevention, and silence/music fixtures. The local evaluation covered four recordings and 68 reviewed boundaries, with median boundary error of 0.42 seconds; two low-confidence music sections remained poor.
claims.limits: This was a local pilot evaluation, not evidence for all 12 recordings or visitor outcomes.

claims.statement: Contributor 07 found that the confidence threshold was embedded in code and source-paragraph provenance was missing; Contributor 01 corrected this by making the threshold configurable at a 0.72 default, adding paragraph index and audio offset, and adding a legacy-timestamp regression fixture.
claims.limits: A further reply beneath Contributor 01's correction remained uninspected at the source-call ceiling, so later review disposition is unknown.

claims.statement: Contributor 03 corrected transcript sentence splits and supplied reference boundaries; Contributor 01 regenerated cues and investigated flags. Contributor 08 supported export, Contributor 04 supplied player fixes, Contributor 07 reviewed the tooling, and Contributor 06 controlled release.
claims.limits: These are distinct contributions and should not be collapsed into Contributor 01's personal work.

claims.statement: Contributor 01 detected that recording J's source differed from the brief and withheld validation. Contributor 03 confirmed the brief was stale, replaced the reference points and required the earlier result to be discarded. Contributor 01 then reran J: 15 of 16 boundaries were within one second; the remaining boundary was 1.3 seconds late at 0.61 confidence and was accepted after editorial listening.
claims.limits: This is a single-recording check with an editorial exception, not a general accuracy rate.

claims.statement: Music and overlapping speech remained material limitations. Recording D required a manual split that was explicitly a content judgment rather than a general tool improvement.
claims.limits: The absence of another report during one subsequent shift is not evidence that the problem was permanently eliminated.

claims.statement: Contributor 04, not Contributor 01, diagnosed and repaired player-side flicker and seek-state defects. The seek defect reproduced independently of cue generation; Contributor 01's limited contribution was supplying the recording-B fixture.
claims.limits: These defects should not be attributed to the alignment method or counted as Contributor 01's fixes.

claims.statement: Ten reviewed recordings were released to the spring evening programme and remained there through June; K and L were not completed because their transcripts still lacked curatorial approval.
claims.limits: Release and continued presence do not establish accessibility impact, and the K/L delay was not Contributor 01's responsibility.

claims.statement: Across seven evening sessions, voluntary host logs recorded 11 transcript-related comments from approximately 510 audio starts: five wording requests, three early or late highlights, two larger-text requests and one unclear note; no session was cancelled because of the player.
claims.limits: The logs were voluntary and cannot establish a true visitor error rate or a causal effect of Contributor 01's work.

claims.statement: A contributor used the runbook to generate cues for one staff-training recording outside the pilot; import succeeded after Contributor 08 clarified export. Only flagged sections were reviewed.
claims.limits: This is one reuse event, not evidence of repeated use, full accuracy, permanent-collection adoption or Contributor 01's later ownership.

claims.statement: Two editors reported that the timing workflow reduced preparation effort, but effort was not time-tracked; broader collection adoption and visitor accessibility impact remained unmeasured.
claims.limits: The underlying editor-survey attachment was unavailable, so this rests on the retrospective's summary and is not a quantified causal result.

claims.statement: The pilot's intended result was easier transcript following, explicitly not formal accessibility compliance.
claims.limits: Neither internal staff reactions nor operational logs establish accessibility compliance or visitor benefit.

rejected_conclusions.reason: The release depended on editorial boundaries and decisions, export support, player fixes and programme approval owned by other contributors.

rejected_conclusions.statement: Contributor 01 fixed the tablet flicker and seek-state defects.
rejected_conclusions.reason: Contributor 04 owned and implemented the player fixes; the seek issue reproduced independently of cue generation. Contributor 01 only supplied one fixture.

rejected_conclusions.statement: The prototype validated all 12 recordings or achieved a general 0.42-second error rate.
rejected_conclusions.reason: The 0.42-second median covered four recordings and 68 reviewed boundaries; K and L were never completed, and music/overlap remained difficult.

rejected_conclusions.statement: The project proved accessibility improvement or a low visitor error rate.
rejected_conclusions.reason: The brief disclaimed formal accessibility compliance, the staff walkthrough was not visitor research, and voluntary logs cannot establish a true error rate.

rejected_conclusions.statement: The tooling was broadly adopted after the pilot.
rejected_conclusions.reason: There was one documented reuse outside the pilot; permanent-collection adoption remained undecided and broader adoption unmeasured.

rejected_conclusions.statement: K and L were delayed by Contributor 01.
rejected_conclusions.reason: They were waiting for revised or approved curatorial transcripts.

rejected_conclusions.statement: Recording J's first result was an alignment failure.
rejected_conclusions.reason: The brief named a stale master; the earlier result was explicitly to be discarded and J was rerun against the replacement source.
